# UltraFont **Any font. Everywhere. Verified.**
[![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%2012→17-3DDC84?style=for-the-badge&logo=android&logoColor=white)](#) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/v3.0.0-1A1B27?style=for-the-badge)](../../releases) [![Download](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download-6C5CE7?style=for-the-badge&logo=download&logoColor=white)](../../releases/latest) `Magisk` · `KernelSU` · `KernelSU Next` · `APatch` · `SukiSU`
Drop in any font. Reboot. Your whole phone uses it. Emoji, CJK and scripts your font can't draw stay stock, so nothing turns into empty boxes.
## It tells you if it worked Most font modules copy files and hope your root manager mounts them. When that fails, it fails quietly. Clean log, zero changes, nothing to debug. UltraFont mounts its own files, then checks every one against the live system and writes the answer into your module list. ``` [ ACTIVE ] MyFont.ttf on 71/71 font files. synthetic-bold=1 gms-mask=off ``` Tap **Action** for the full picture: what's live, what stayed stock and why, and what's fighting it.
## Install ``` 1 Download the zip from Releases 2 Manager → Modules → Install from storage 3 Reboot → tap Action ``` > First set your ROM's font picker to **Default** (*Settings → Font style*). > Its overlay sits above system fonts and beats every module. **New font later?** Drop it in `/data/adb/modules/ultrafont/fonts/`, delete the old one, reboot. No reflash. Add `Bold.ttf` · `Italic.ttf` · `Medium.ttf` to fill those weights.
## Settings `/data/adb/ultrafont.conf` — edit, reboot. | | | | |:--|:--|:--| | `SYNTH_BOLD` | `auto` | Fixes bold rendering flat | | `CLEAR_UPDATED_FONTS` | `1` | Clears `/data/fonts`, which beats every module | | `SELF_MOUNT` | `1` | Mount our own files | | `SCRIPT_FALLBACKS` | `auto` | `auto` · `off` · `"bengali thai"` | | `REPLACE_MONO` | `1` | Replace monospace | | `MASK_GMS_FONTS` | `0` | Move Google apps onto your font |
## Under the hood **Font Doctor** reads your font's own `cmap` table on the device and measures what it can actually draw. A script's fallback gets replaced only if your font covers it. Everything skipped records a reason like `no-thai-glyphs`. **Bold that works.** Android 12+ ships a variable Roboto and asks it for weight 700. A static font can't answer, so every heading renders flat. `SYNTH_BOLD` rewrites a copy of your own font config so Android synthesises it instead. **Can't brick you.** Counts boots, drops the risky part after one failure, disables itself after three.
## Something off? | Symptom | Fix | |:--|:--| | Nothing changed | ROM font picker → **Default** | | Bold looks like regular | `SYNTH_BOLD=1` | | Only Google apps unchanged | `MASK_GMS_FONTS=1` | | Boxes in one language | Working as intended, see `skipped.txt` | | `0` live in the report | Check `SELF_MOUNT=1`, read `boot.log` |
Flow
``` install analyse font → build tree → flag conflicts post-fs-data rebuild if changed → clear /data/fonts → bind-mount → verify zygote every app inherits it boot completed write status line ```

---
**Mohammad Mehrab Hossain** · [`0xmehr4b`](https://github.com/0xmehr4b) [Docs](module/README.txt) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Credits](CREDITS.md) · [Licence](LICENSE)

UltraFont

Any font. Everywhere. Verified.


![Android](#)

![Version](../../releases)

![Download](../../releases/latest)

Magisk · KernelSU · KernelSU Next · APatch · SukiSU


Drop in any font. Reboot. Your whole phone uses it.

Emoji, CJK and scripts your font can't draw stay stock, so nothing turns into

empty boxes.


It tells you if it worked

Most font modules copy files and hope your root manager mounts them. When that

fails, it fails quietly. Clean log, zero changes, nothing to debug.

UltraFont mounts its own files, then checks every one against the live system

and writes the answer into your module list.

[ ACTIVE ]  MyFont.ttf on 71/71 font files.  synthetic-bold=1  gms-mask=off

Tap Action for the full picture: what's live, what stayed stock and why, and

what's fighting it.


Install

1  Download the zip from Releases
2  Manager → Modules → Install from storage
3  Reboot → tap Action

> First set your ROM's font picker to Default (*Settings → Font style*).

> Its overlay sits above system fonts and beats every module.

New font later? Drop it in /data/adb/modules/ultrafont/fonts/, delete the

old one, reboot. No reflash. Add Bold.ttf · Italic.ttf · Medium.ttf to

fill those weights.


Settings

/data/adb/ultrafont.conf — edit, reboot.

| | | |

|:--|:--|:--|

| SYNTH_BOLD | auto | Fixes bold rendering flat |

| CLEAR_UPDATED_FONTS | 1 | Clears /data/fonts, which beats every module |

| SELF_MOUNT | 1 | Mount our own files |

| SCRIPT_FALLBACKS | auto | auto · off · "bengali thai" |

| REPLACE_MONO | 1 | Replace monospace |

| MASK_GMS_FONTS | 0 | Move Google apps onto your font |


Under the hood

Font Doctor reads your font's own cmap table on the device and measures

what it can actually draw. A script's fallback gets replaced only if your font

covers it. Everything skipped records a reason like no-thai-glyphs.

Bold that works. Android 12+ ships a variable Roboto and asks it for weight

  • A static font can't answer, so every heading renders flat. `SYNTH_BOLD`

    • rewrites a copy of your own font config so Android synthesises it instead.

    Can't brick you. Counts boots, drops the risky part after one failure,

    disables itself after three.


    Something off?

    | Symptom | Fix |

    |:--|:--|

    | Nothing changed | ROM font picker → Default |

    | Bold looks like regular | SYNTH_BOLD=1 |

    | Only Google apps unchanged | MASK_GMS_FONTS=1 |

    | Boxes in one language | Working as intended, see skipped.txt |

    | 0 live in the report | Check SELF_MOUNT=1, read boot.log |


    Flow


    install         analyse font → build tree → flag conflicts
post-fs-data    rebuild if changed → clear /data/fonts
                → bind-mount → verify
zygote          every app inherits it
boot completed  write status line


    ---

    Mohammad Mehrab Hossain · 0xmehr4b

    Docs · Changelog · Credits · Licence
